name: שֶׁאֱרָה
summary: A daughter of the house of Ephraim, named after Beriah, who built Lower and Upper Beth-horon and Uzzen-sheerah, the town that bears her name (1Ch 7:23–24). She is named only there. The name has the letters of שְׁאֵר and its feminine שַׁאֲרָה “blood relation” (Lev 18:17), and also of שְׁאָר “remnant”; Beriah was named “because it went evil with his house” after his brothers were killed (1Ch 7:21–23), which would suit either. Scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “His daughter was Sheerah (שֶׁאֱרָה), who built Beth-horon the lower and the upper, and Uzzen-sheerah.”
Ephraim's son Beriah, “because it went evil with his house”.
The men of Gath killed Ephraim's sons Ezer and Elead.
“They are near kin (שַׁאֲרָה הֵנָּה)”: the feminine noun whose letters the name shares.

note: Takes v.al.ad, two tokens in 1Ch 7:24: the woman and the second element of the place name Uzzen-sheerah, which has no entry. Whose daughter she is (Ephraim's or Beriah's) the verse leaves open; TIPNR makes her Beriah's. The pointing שֶׁאֱרָה is not that of שַׁאֲרָה or שְׁאֵרִית, so the meaning is only the root's; no verse or cognate fixes it.
